clue.text: Doorstepper alert (funny?) — but neither Neil nor Glenys get in

indicators.note: neither ... get in says the two letters are kept out of the first surname

parts.note: Neil Kinnock, former leader of the UK Labour Party
taken as written: the letters that do not get in

indicators.note: nor continues the same idea: the second surname also loses those two letters

parts.note: Glenys Kinnock, Labour politician and wife of Neil

explanation.surface: A comic warning about someone at the door, with a jibe at the Kinnocks being kept out of office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neither' and 'nor' each take IN out of KINNOCK, leaving KNOCK twice. Neil and Glenys Kinnock were a well-known British Labour political couple.
explanation.definitionFit: The joke format opens with a caller rapping at the door, so the phrase is a doorstep warning that a gag is coming.

clue.text: Vineyard out of Santa Cruz in new production lines

indicators.note: a new production rearranges the remaining letters into fresh order
out of says the vineyard's letters are removed from the place name

parts.note: a cru is a vineyard or wine-growing estate, especially in France

explanation.surface: A Californian winery mounting a fresh show, with a line of verse thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' takes CRU from SANTACRUZ, leaving SANTAZ, which 'new production' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanza is a group of verse lines forming a unit of a poem.

clue.text: Toast ox cryptically in desert?

indicators.note: in places the second piece inside the first

parts.note: to desert is to forsake
read cryptically, O is old (as in O for old) and X is the times sign

explanation.surface: A puzzling question about raising a glass to an ox in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptically' tells you to read the letters of 'ox' as symbols: O is a standard abbreviation for old, and X is the multiplication sign, read as 'times'. 'in' does the containment.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a common toast drunk in memory of shared past days.

clue.text: Discover good news for England's opposition at Lord's?

definitions.text: good news for England's opposition at Lord's
definitions.meaning: Joe Root, England's star batsman, being dismissed at Lord's, the London cricket ground, pleases the other team

explanation.surface: Finding out what cheers England's opponents at a Lord's Test match.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is a London cricket ground; Joe Root is an England batsman, so 'Root out' is his dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: To root out is to dig up or uncover something hidden, a synonym of discover.

clue.text: Move dangerously to shatter teenage romance?

indicators.note: shattering breaks the words up so their letters can be reassembled

explanation.surface: Reckless behaviour that wrecks a young couple's relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to shatter' rearranges MOVEDANGEROUSLY into the fifteen letters of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Love's young dream is the idealised first love of youth, an idiom for a youthful romance.

clue.text: Second collection of ashes causing sorrow

parts.note: MO is a short moment, as in 'half a mo'
an urnful is as much as an urn holds, such as cremated ashes

explanation.surface: A second funeral urn brings fresh grief.
explanation.definitionFit: Mournful describes something sad that brings grief, matching the sense of causing sorrow.

clue.text: Advertise to promote Spar

definitions.meaning: to ... a product is to push it hard
a spar along the foot of a sail

explanation.surface: Run adverts for the Spar convenience-store chain.
explanation.walkthrough: Spar is a chain of convenience stores, but here it is the sailing pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Boom covers publicising loudly and also the horizontal pole holding a sail's lower edge.

clue.text: Testing on-field exchange

definitions.meaning: '...' is said when testing a microphone
a quick give-and-go pass between two footballers

explanation.surface: A trial move swapped between players during a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound engineers count aloud to check a mic, and footballers trade a wall pass called by the same name.

clue.text: Return average toffee drinks

indicators.note: return means the combined pieces are read backwards

parts.note: so-so means average or middling
Rolo is a brand of chocolate-covered toffee sweet

explanation.surface: Sending back a mediocre sweet and some drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Rolo is a well-known British chocolate-coated toffee sweet. 'Return' reverses both pieces together, so the toffee ends up at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Oloroso is a dark, rich style of sherry, so these are glasses of fortified wine.

clue.text: Suspect: "I'm scot-free" — hence not returning to it?

definitions.text: Suspect: "I'm scot-free" — hence not returning to it?

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, so these letters are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: A suspect who got off declares freedom and so won't revisit where it happened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' rearranges IMSCOTFREEHENCE. The whole clue also plays on the saying that a criminal always returns to the scene of the crime.
explanation.definitionFit: The place where an offence occurred is where a guilty party is proverbially drawn back.

clue.text: Part of the ceremonial Celtic attire of Treliske and Hugus

definitions.text: Part of the ceremonial Celtic attire

indicators.note: of here means the answer is taken from within the following words, spanning them

explanation.surface: A Highland-dress item belonging to two Cornish places near Truro.
explanation.walkthrough: Treliske and Hugus are places in Cornwall; the answer spans 'TreliSKE AND HUgus'.
explanation.definitionFit: A skean-dhu is the small dagger tucked into the sock as part of Scottish Highland dress.

clue.text: Fairies got over woodpecker

indicators.note: over in a down-the-page sense signals the letters are turned back to front

parts.note: ELF and FAY are both fairies

explanation.surface: Some fairies recovered from a woodpecker's attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns ELF + FAY back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Yaffle is a dialect name for the green woodpecker, from its laughing call.

clue.text: Character-forming interpretation for Spooner to tear up

indicators.note: Spooner's name signals swapping the opening sounds of two words

parts.note: to tear is to rip
up means ahead, leading

explanation.surface: A reading that builds character, which Spooner would rather destroy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for Spooner' swaps the first letters of RIP LEADING. 'up' means ahead, as in a team leading.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip-reading interprets speech from the shapes the mouth makes as it forms each sound.

clue.text: City troubled after rolling my film

indicators.note: after puts the city behind the turned exclamation
rolling turns the exclamation over so it reads backwards

parts.note: cor and my are both exclamations of surprise
Kyiv, the war-torn Ukrainian capital

explanation.surface: A city in turmoil after some upheaval, over a cry about a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' is the exclamation of surprise, not the possessive; 'rolling' reverses it. 'troubled' describes the war-hit Ukrainian capital rather than signalling an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocky IV is the 1985 boxing movie starring Sylvester Stallone, fourth in its series.

clue.text: Talked-about international lived for spinning? Yes and no

definitions.text: Talked-about international lived for spinning? Yes and no

indicators.note: talked about says the word is heard, not seen, so its spelling may differ

parts.note: a cap is a player picked for a national team

indicators.note: spinning sends the letters of the word lived round into a new order

explanation.surface: A celebrated cricketer whose life revolved around spin, or did it?
explanation.walkthrough: 'for spinning' rearranges LIVED into ILDEV. 'Yes and no' because Kapil Dev was a fast-medium bowler, yet his name does involve spinning.
explanation.definitionFit: Kapil Dev is the famous Indian all-rounder who captained India to the 1983 World Cup.

clue.text: Two of the same please, landlord, for singer and songwriter

parts.note: dual means twofold, a pair of the same
IPA, India pale ale, is the beer ordered from the pub landlord

explanation.surface: Ordering a pair of drinks at the bar for a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: A pub landlord is the person behind the bar who serves the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dua Lipa is the British pop star who writes and performs hits such as Levitating.

clue.text: Do a class

parts.note: a, as in 'once a day', means per
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: Run a lesson or go to a school class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' means 'each', as in a pound a head, which is PER.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something, such as a song or task, is to carry it out, which is what perform means.

clue.text: The first of practical jokes played around city

indicators.note: around says the reworked word encloses the single letter
played means the letters of jokes are toyed with and moved about
the first of means the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: Pranks were carried out around town, beginning with practical jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' rearranges JOKES as SKOJE; 'around' puts P inside, after the O.
explanation.definitionFit: Skopje is the capital city of North Macedonia.

clue.text: Weighted rent, ignoring the shackles of age

indicators.note: shackles go on the extremities, so ignoring them drops each word's outer letters

explanation.surface: A tenant's adjusted rent, freed from limits based on age.
explanation.definitionFit: Eighteen is a person's age at adulthood in the UK, so a number of years fits age.

clue.text: Gushing report of degree class

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the answer is the sound of the degree grade

parts.note: a 2:2, a 'two-two', is a lower second-class British degree

explanation.surface: An effusive write-up of how well someone did in their degree.
explanation.walkthrough: British degrees are graded first, 2:1, 2:2 and third; a 2:2 is spoken 'two-two'.
explanation.definitionFit: Too-too means excessively affected or effusive, an old-fashioned word for over-the-top.

clue.text: After resignation of Hammerstein, Rodgers this gobsmacked?

definitions.text: After resignation of Hammerstein, Rodgers this
definitions.meaning: Hammerstein wrote the lyrics in Rodgers and Hammerstein, so without him Rodgers would lack words

explanation.surface: Rodgers stunned when his songwriting partner Hammerstein quits.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Rodgers wrote the music and Oscar Hammerstein the lyrics of shows such as Oklahoma!
explanation.definitionFit: Being stunned into silence leaves one unable to speak, the idiom's everyday sense.

clue.text: All the best art at auction houses

indicators.note: houses says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Good wishes for paintings going under the hammer at sale rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Ta-ta is a casual British goodbye, a farewell like wishing someone well.

clue.text: With a single dash, we see him lose his get-up-and-go!

definitions.text: With a single dash, we see him lose his get-up-and-go!

parts.words: With a single dash, we see him lose his get-up-and-go!
parts.note: a naked runner dashes across, having shed his outfit, his get-up

explanation.surface: A runner's burst of speed exhausting his energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get-up' is clothing, not energy, and the dash is a sprint across a pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A streaker runs naked through a public place, often a sports field.

clue.text: All the drinks one's got in local

definitions.text: All the drinks one's got in
definitions.meaning: a round is the set of drinks bought for a group, with A

explanation.surface: Buying drinks for everybody at the neighbourhood pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' looks like a pub, the British sense, but it means nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Around describes something close at hand, in the vicinity.
